thread:
alice nguyen: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a concrete plan for backfilling private peering vs using the ephemeral route allocator for long-lived customers. Thoughts?
ben choi: Agree we should pick one pattern per customer cohort. Backfill peering is simpler for large enterprise but painful ops-wise.
carla mendez: What about a hybrid: peering for customers with strict egress IP SLAs, ephemeral allocator for others. We need clear triggers. :thinking:
eva singh: Triggers = commit size (reserved capacity), SLA tier, and regulatory flag. If reserved >= X GPUs or monthly spend >= $Y => require peering.
frank r: Ops concerns: peering increases NAT and route table churn. Migration risk during cutover. Ephemeral allocator keeps control plane simple but breaks src-ip preservation.
alice nguyen: Exactly — src-ip preservation is the customer ask for egress allowlists. Can we emulate with SNAT and floating IPs from an IP pool?
danny opsbot: infra-bot note: current allocator gives ephemeral IPs with TTL 1h, no affinity guarantees. We can extend TTL + sticky leases per customer.
carla mendez: Sticky leases help, but customers want stable 1-2 static IPs for allowlisting. Sticky lease pool might be acceptable if we guarantee N static leases per account.
eva singh: SLA contract implication: static leases = reserved IP allocation per customer; bill or include in Dedicated pricing.
frank r: Migration playbook (rough): 1) enable sticky lease for customer, 2) assign 2 static IPs, advertise to customer, 3) validate traffic, 4) cut traffic path to peering if requested. Need rollback path.
alice nguyen: For peering cutover we must ensure control plane separation doesn't break agent handshake. Two concerns: certificate propagation and route advertisement timing.
eva singh: Suggestion: introduce a short-lived 'shadow-peering' mode where we mirror egress both via allocator and peering for 24-48h and compare metrics. Then silently shift DNS/route preference.
carla mendez: Mirror mode is good but doubles egress cost during window. We should gate it to high-value customers only.
frank r: Also add health checks: validate TCP/443 flow and source IP consistency at edge. If mismatch, auto rollback.
danny opsbot: example operator config snippet for sticky leases / mirror mode:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: EgressPolicy
metadata:
  tenant: acme-corp
spec:
  mode: sticky-leases
  leases: 2
  leaseTTL: 30d
  mirrorToPeering: true
  mirrorDuration: 48h
```
carla mendez: That looks fine. Need to ensure the lease allocator can export assignments to the control plane and persist across agent restarts.
eva singh: Dataflow: allocator -> controlplane -> customer config UI. Traceability + audit log required for compliance.
alice nguyen: Rollout plan idea: 1) implement sticky leases behind feature flag, 2) onboard pilot customer, 3) add mirror mode and analytics, 4) formalize peering cutover playbook.
frank r: Edge case: failover when peering experiences packet loss. We must have automatic fallback to allocator to avoid customer downtime. Circuit-breaker semantics.
carla mendez: Agree — define SLO thresholds that trigger fallback and a cooldown window. Document deterministic owner for each step.
eva singh: Questions for legal/compliance: are sticky ips considered still under our IP namespace? Need to include in contract addendum.
alice nguyen: Action items: @ben will draft the migration playbook, @carla will spec allocator persistence, @eva will draft SLA language, @frank will design health-check circuit-breaker. I can coordinate pilot. :thumbsup:
ben choi: On it. I'll post a first-draft checklist by tomorrow.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Feature flag toggled for sticky-lease prototype on staging (ff/sticky-lease)
frank r: One more ask — add telemetry: per-tenant egress path (peering vs allocator), latency, packet loss, cost delta. Need this for monthly review.
alice nguyen: Good call. We'll reconvene after ben's checklist. Thanks everyone.
extra_notes: Thread follows RFC on private connectivity; not a formal decision — action items created to scope prototype.
